title: CREDIT DECISION AUTOMATION IN COMMERCIAL BANKS: A REVIEW OF AI AND PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS IN LOAN ASSESSMENT
authors: Kowsar, M. M.; Mohiuddin, M.; Mohna, H. A.
tldr: AI and predictive analytics, especially ensemble and deep learning models, outperform traditional methods in credit scoring accuracy, reduce processing time and costs, and expand credit access via alternative data, but raise ethical and regulatory concerns around bias and explainability.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional credit assessment is time-consuming, subjective, and inconsistent. There is a growing need for more efficient, accurate, and inclusive loan evaluation processes. AI and predictive analytics offer a potential solution, but their integration raises concerns about bias, transparency, and regulation.
approach: Conducted a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines.
Searched Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for studies from 2000 to 2023.
Selected 102 peer-reviewed studies focusing on AI or predictive analytics in credit scoring.
Extracted data on authorship, methodology, AI techniques, data types, and evaluation metrics.
Performed a narrative synthesis organized thematically around key domains.
Included studies covering both developed and developing market contexts.
Evaluated findings on predictive accuracy, operational efficiency, and financial inclusion.
Analyzed the literature for ethical, regulatory, and explainability considerations.
findings: num: 78 of 86 comparison studies found AI models outperformed traditional methods in AUC, Gini, and default prediction.
num: Ensemble models like XGBoost and random forests consistently improved risk segmentation across diverse datasets.
num: Loan processing time was reduced by 60–80% with real-time AI-based scoring.
num: Some banks reported saving 20–35% in loan origination costs after full automation.
num: Automated systems handled loan volumes 10–15 times higher than manual processes.
num: Approval rates for thin-file applicants rose by 25–40% using alternative data.
num: Inclusion-focused AI models achieved a repayment rate above 90% in over 20 studies.
num: AI automation investments were recouped within 1–2 years, often yielding up to 5x returns.
Ethical concerns and explainability limitations were recurrent in 48 of the reviewed studies.
The use of alternative data like mobile metadata and psychometric tests expanded credit access to underserved groups.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic review synthesizes a broad body of literature on AI-driven credit automation, providing a comprehensive overview of methodological advancements, operational impacts, and ethical challenges. It consolidates evidence that AI models, particularly ensembles and deep learning, offer significant predictive advantages over traditional methods. The review also critically examines the role of alternative data in expanding financial inclusion and the corresponding need for robust governance frameworks. By identifying key research gaps in transparency, bias mitigation, and real-time adaptability, it serves as a foundational resource for future studies and policy development in algorithmic credit assessment.
directly_justifies: AI models, especially ensembles, consistently outperform traditional credit scoring in accuracy.
Real-time scoring and RPA reduce loan processing time by 60-80% and costs by 20-35%.
Alternative data like mobile metadata and psychometric tests expands credit access to underserved groups.
Automation investments are recouped within 1-2 years, yielding up to 5x returns.
Explainability and fairness remain critical challenges for AI adoption in credit.
limits: The paper is a systematic review, not an empirical study, so its findings are aggregations of others' work.
It focuses on commercial banking, with limited discussion of personal finance management systems.
The review does not provide specific comparative analysis for the Filipino context.
While it discusses alternative data, it does not evaluate the effectiveness of specific cultural or seasonal spending patterns.
The paper does not address system-level design constraints like mobile-first or offline-first architectures.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan was conducted across all topic domains in the taxonomy. Domains 4.A and 4.B (Landscape and Limitations of Existing Systems) were flagged as high relevance because the paper reviews and critiques current AI-driven credit systems. Domains 6.A and 6.B (Predictive Modeling and Forecasting) were also high, as predictive analytics is the paper's core subject. Domains 12.A and 12.B (Evaluation Frameworks) were high, as the review compares model performance using standard metrics. Domain 5.C (Classification Approaches) was medium, as the paper discusses borrower segmentation but not as a primary focus. Domains 10.A and 10.B (Privacy and Trust) were medium, as they are important but not the central theme. Domain 1.B (Financial Structure), 1.C (Behavior), 7.A (Budgeting), and 12.C (Budget Evaluation) were considered contextual due to indirect links. Domain 8.A (Anomaly Detection) was low, as it is only briefly mentioned. The paper is not specific to Filipino young professionals or their spending practices, so those topics were rejected. Overall, the paper's topical coverage is strongest in predictive modeling, system evaluation, and the challenges of current financial systems.

limitations: Systematic review methodology limits causal inference and independent validation. [unacknowledged]
Limited discussion on the long-term operational sustainability and maintenance of AI systems. [unacknowledged]
Potentially over-relies on studies from developed markets, which may not fully generalize to developing contexts. [unacknowledged]
The review does not address the potential for model drift over time in dynamic credit environments. [unacknowledged]
Selection bias may exist as the review excludes non-English and unpublished studies.
remember_this: Ensemble models (XGBoost, random forests) outperform traditional methods in default prediction.
AI automation reduces loan processing time by 60-80% and origination costs by 20-35%.
Alternative data expands credit access to thin-file populations with repayment rates above 90%.
Explainability and bias mitigation are crucial challenges for AI adoption in credit.
ROI from credit automation is typically realized within 1-2 years, yielding up to 5x returns.
